summary: Connect native analytic collision, persistent contact scheduling and Coulomb TGS into resident multi-frame 3D ball/box scene programs.
regressions: Fourteen live native scenes cover empty/static inputs, impacts, falling bodies, sliding-to-rolling friction, ball/box stacks, 120-frame persistence, interleaved batches and lane tails.
Exact guards, IDs, contact ordering, adjacency ownership, color conflicts, bucket bijections, state persistence and copied bits are validated independently of floating-point comparisons.
Independent finite/unit-rotation/static-body, penetration, energy, restitution, rolling and settling assertions apply to the saved checkpoints; matching invalid native/target output is rejected.
differences: This is an explicit analytic ordinary-body scope, with eight buckets and sixteen bounded Topo rounds; unsolved contacts reject scene acceptance. Joints, hubs, generic collision and production public backend selection remain unfinished.
The fixture oracle reuses extracted native dispatch controllers for radix, buckets and coloring; no native physics equations are duplicated into Python.

Only multi-frame cached warmstart velocity diagnostics use 1e-5 absolute tolerance, justified by 2.744e-6 near-zero angular-cache drift after 120 box-stack frames; body errors remain below the existing 2e-6/2e-5 bounds and physical checks pass. Isolated kernel tolerances and the zero-distance release block are unchanged.
Scene workspace beyond its current published range may contain preceding-frame allocations. Maximum-capacity guards, read-only data and every live identity remain exact.
Ascend results can establish source lowering only; vendor compilation and execution remain unavailable.
